question: In the context of the preparation of the forthcoming Biotech Act II, and considering that agriculture constitutes the foundational input for a resilient and competitive European bioeconomy, how does the Commission intend to ensure that the proposal goes beyond a narrow focus on industrial biotechnology and biomanufacturing to fully integrate agricultural biotechnology, including plant and microbial innovations?

Can the Commission commit to undertaking a comprehensive assessment of the full horizontal biotechnology framework (notably Directives 2001/18/EC1 and 2009/41/EC2 and Regulation (EC) No 1829/20033) and to identify and address regulatory bottlenecks to ensure a predictable, science-based pathway to market for these critical technologies?
Can the Commission also commit to simultaneously improving societal dialogue about these technologies and their benefits with a view to strengthening public trust?

Directive 2001/18/EC of the European Parliament and of the Council of 12 March 2001 on the deliberate release into the environment of genetically modified organisms (ELI: http://data.europa.eu/eli/dir/2001/18/oj). 2 Directive 2009/41/EC of the European Parliament and of the Council of 6 May 2009 on the contained use of genetically modified micro-organisms (ELI: http://data.europa.eu/eli/dir/2009/41/oj).
3 Regulation (EC) No 1829/2003 of the European Parliament and of the Council of 22 September 2003 on genetically modified food and feed (ELI: http://data.europa.eu/eli/reg/2003/1829/oj). 1
answer: The Commission will ensure an ambitious proposal for the Biotech Act II, aiming to enhance the EU’s industrial competitiveness in industrial biotechnology and biomanufacturing. This includes increasing the resilience of the EU single market and promoting EU-based sustainable production. The exact scope of the act will be determined based on the impact assessment, including stakeholders’ feedback (1).

The Commission proposed a regulation (2) and a directive (3) adopted on 16 December 2025 as the European Biotech Act, which covers food biotechnology by proposing amendments to the General Food Law (4), including some measures also applicable to genetically modified food and feed regulated under Regulation (EC) No 1829/2003 (5).

In addition, targeted amendments to Directive 2001/18/EC (6) are intended to reduce administrative burdens for microbial innovations in the agricultural and other sectors and enhance the EU's global competitiveness . The Commission remains committed to ensuring support for the scale-up of all biotechnologies.

A full mapping of regulatory bottlenecks related to biotechnology has been conducted in an external study commissioned by the Commission (7), which will be published on the website of the Directorate-General for Internal Market, Industry, Entrepreneurship and SMEs by the end of September 2026 (8) .
The Commission recognises the importance of an informed societal dialogue on new technologies and their potential benefits.
